summary: Checks whether a value is **not** `null` or `undefined`.
description: `nonNil(value)` is the same test as `!isNil(value)`, written so that a guard clause reads as a sentence rather than as a negation.
The absent values, and only those: `0`, `""` and `false` are present values and do not qualify.
`isX` and `nonX` answer a question and never interrupt control flow; `requireX` and `requireNonX` hand the value back or throw. The scheme is explained in [](validation-conventions.md).
returns: `true` when the value is not `null` or `undefined`; otherwise `false`.

examples.title: What passes and what does not
examples.body:
```javascript
nonNil(0); // => true
nonNil(""); // => true
nonNil(false); // => true
nonNil(null); // => false
nonNil(undefined); // => false
```
